keyTerms.definition: Layers run input to prediction; then loss, backprop, activations.
Survives training; with checkpointing trading compute for memory.

recall.question: What is the climb order?
recall.answer: One neuron, then a layer, then the forward pass, loss, backprop, activations, then optimizers, normalization, initialization.

keyTerms.definition: The smallest learnable unit: weights times inputs, plus bias.
A number the network learns; sets how much an input matters.
A learned offset added to the weighted sum.
Why a neuron needs one; what breaks without it.

recall.question: What does a neuron compute, exactly?
recall.answer: It multiplies each input by its own weight, adds the results plus one learned bias.

recall.question: Where does everything a trained network 'knows' live?

sections.title: Chapter 2: Layers and the Forward Pass

keyTerms.definition: Many neurons side by side, all reading the same inputs.
Running input through layers to prediction.
What a neural network computationally is.

recall.question: What does a layer add that a single neuron cannot?
recall.answer: Multiple boundaries: many neurons side by side with their own weights.

sections.title: Chapter 3: Loss: How the Network Knows It Is Wrong

keyTerms.definition: Turns a prediction and its answer into one number: how wrong.
What the number lives on; training walks it.

recall.question: Why do regression and classification use different losses?
recall.answer: Different output types need different wrongness measures.

keyTerms.definition: What assigns blame to individual weights.
Why gradient computation runs backward.
The training loop: which knob to turn, and which way.

recall.question: How does the network know which weight to blame?
recall.answer: The chain rule: gradients flow backward assigning blame to each weight.

keyTerms.definition: The default hidden activation.
Squashes into (0,1).
Squashes into (-1,1); zero-centered.
Turns raw scores into probabilities.
What it is and saturation.

recall.question: Why is ReLU the default hidden activation?
recall.answer: The bend matters; the chapter explains why against sigmoid/tanh saturation.

keyTerms.definition: What Adam does that SGD does not, part one.
Per-parameter step sizes; part two.
Decoupled weight decay; different from Adam with weight decay on.

recall.question: When would you still pick SGD with momentum over Adam?
recall.answer: The chapter's design prompt; weigh generalization against adaptivity.

keyTerms.definition: Re-centers and re-scales activations at every layer.
Versus layer norm; the design prompt compares.

recall.question: Why do deep stacks need normalization?
recall.answer: Signal scale drifts through dozens of layers; activations grow or shrink, gradients follow, training stalls or explodes.

keyTerms.definition: Weight scale before the first step decides if any signal survives.
N(0,1) weights in a 30-layer network; ReLU needs different scale than tanh.

recall.question: Why can you not initialize all weights to zero?
recall.answer: Symmetry never breaks; no signal differentiation.

recall.question: How do you diagnose a dead network at initialization?
recall.answer: Check forward signal stats; the chapter's design prompt.

keyTerms.definition: 16-bit float; range versus precision tradeoff against BF16.
Brain float 16; different range-precision tradeoff.
Fixes what breaks in FP16.
Why they live in FP32.

recall.question: Why train in 16 bits at all?
recall.answer: Faster compute and half the bytes moved; spend bits where they matter.

keyTerms.definition: Forget most activations, recompute on backward; trades compute for memory.
At long sequences they dwarf the weights.

recall.question: What eats more memory: weights or activations?
recall.answer: At long sequences, the activations saved for backward dwarf the weights.

recall.question: What does checkpointing not save?
recall.answer: The chapter's design prompt; know the limits.

keyTerms.definition: An information wall: the model never received what is outside the window.
Builds the architecture that crosses this wall.

recall.question: What breaks first when sequences get long?
recall.answer: Information: a fixed window cannot read a long document no matter the tuning.

keyTerms.definition: Volume 4: this diagram built at scale, on sequences.
Neurons and layers become these inside the transformer.

recall.question: How does every piece slot into the transformer?
recall.answer: Neurons become MLP blocks, loss-to-optimizers the training loop, norm plus init signal control, precision and checkpointing the scale budget.
